method: AI-assisted comparison against the saved expected_behavior per requirement. Review considers unsupported expected outcomes, coverage, contradictions and usable fixtures. Prompt outputs are proposals, not executed product tests.

cases.requirement: An active registered user requests a password reset. Send a single-use link to their verified email. The link is valid for 15 minutes and expires at 15 minutes. A valid link lets the user set a new password. After success, the old password no longer works and the user must log in again.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover link delivery, a valid reset, expiry just before and at 15 minutes, reuse after success, rejection of the old password and no automatic login. Ask about password rules if needed; do not invent them.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing the core password reset flow, including link validity, expiration, and post-reset authentication behavior. No major gaps prevent proposing candidate tests.

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Valid link used within time limit | User clicks a valid reset link sent to their verified email and submits a new password within 15 minutes. | New password is set successfully; old password no longer works; user is logged out and must log in again. |
| TC-02 | Negative | Expired link used | User clicks a reset link after 15 minutes have passed since it was sent. | System rejects the link as expired; no password change occurs; user is prompted to request a new reset link. |
| TC-03 | Boundary | Link used at exact expiration | User submits a new password at exactly 15 minutes and 0 seconds after link generation. | System rejects the link as expired (based on "expires at 15 minutes" interpretation); no password change occurs. |
| TC-04 | Negative | Reuse of single-use link | User successfully resets password using a valid link, then attempts to use the same link again. | System rejects the link as already used; no password change occurs. |
| TC-05 | Negative | Unverified email address | User requests a password reset for an account with an unverified email address. | System does not send a reset link (or sends a generic message not revealing account existence); no reset link is generated. |
| TC-06 | Normal | Login with old password after reset | User attempts to log in with the old password immediately after successfully resetting it. | Login fails; system prompts for correct credentials. |
| TC-07 | Normal | Login with new password after reset | User attempts to log in with the new password immediately after successfully resetting it. | Login succeeds; user is authenticated. |
| TC-08 | Negative | Invalid email address | User requests a password reset using an email address not associated with any account. | System does not send a reset link; response does not reveal whether the email is registered. |

Questions, if needed
- What is the exact behavior when a user requests a reset for an unverified email? Should the system send a verification email instead, or simply reject the request?
- Is there a rate limit on how many reset links can be requested per user or IP address?

cases.review_notes: Adds unsupported outcomes for unverified or unregistered email addresses and response secrecy.

cases.requirement: A guest can use a cart. Adding a new product sets quantity to 1; adding it again increases quantity by 1. Quantities are whole numbers from 1 to 10. Updating to 0 removes the product. Other invalid quantities are rejected without changing the cart. Total equals unit price times quantity, summed across items; no tax, shipping or discounts apply.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover guest access, first and repeat addition, quantity updates, removal at zero, invalid quantities and recalculated totals. Use labelled example prices with correct arithmetic. Do not require login.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing core cart logic, though it lacks specific details on how "invalid" quantities (e.g., non-integers, negatives) are communicated to the user (error message vs. silent ignore).

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Add new product | Add Product A (Unit Price: $10) | Cart contains Product A with Quantity 1; Total is $10. |
| TC-02 | Normal | Add existing product | Add Product A again | Cart contains Product A with Quantity 2; Total is $20. |
| TC-03 | Boundary | Max quantity limit | Set Product A quantity to 10 | Cart contains Product A with Quantity 10; Total is $100. |
| TC-04 | Boundary | Exceed max quantity | Set Product A quantity to 11 | Quantity remains 10 (or previous valid value); Total unchanged; Invalid input rejected. |
| TC-05 | Boundary | Min quantity limit | Set Product A quantity to 1 | Cart contains Product A with Quantity 1; Total is $10. |
| TC-06 | Negative | Remove product via zero | Set Product A quantity to 0 | Product A is removed from cart; Total is $0 (or sum of remaining items). |
| TC-07 | Negative | Invalid negative quantity | Set Product A quantity to -1 | Quantity remains unchanged; Total unchanged; Invalid input rejected. |
| TC-08 | Negative | Invalid non-integer quantity | Set Product A quantity to 1.5 | Quantity remains unchanged; Total unchanged; Invalid input rejected. |
| TC-09 | Normal | Multiple items total | Add Product A ($10, Qty 2) and Product B ($5, Qty 3) | Total is $35 ($20 + $15). |
| TC-10 | Normal | Update quantity mid-cart | Change Product A quantity from 2 to 5 | Product A Quantity is 5; Total recalculated based on new quantity. |

Questions, if needed
1. How should the system respond to invalid quantity inputs (e.g., -1, 11, 1.5)? Should it display a specific error message, or simply ignore the input?
2. Is there a maximum limit on the number of distinct products in the cart?

cases.review_notes: Covers cart arithmetic and quantity boundaries, but lacks an explicit guest-access check.

cases.requirement: An upload accepts PDF files only, with a maximum size of 5,000,000 bytes inclusive. Empty files are rejected. A rejected file must not be stored. Other file-validation rules are outside this requirement.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover a non-empty PDF below and exactly at the limit, a PDF one byte above it, an empty PDF and a non-PDF. Rejected files must not be stored. Do not invent MIME-detection methods or error wording.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing file type, size, and empty file validation. The main gap is the specific error message or status code expected for rejections, which is not defined.

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Valid PDF within size limit | Upload a 100 KB PDF file | File is accepted and stored |
| TC-02 | Boundary | PDF at maximum size | Upload a PDF file exactly 5,000,000 bytes in size | File is accepted and stored |
| TC-03 | Boundary | PDF exceeding maximum size | Upload a PDF file 5,000,001 bytes in size | File is rejected and not stored |
| TC-04 | Negative | Non-PDF file type | Upload a 100 KB .txt file | File is rejected and not stored |
| TC-05 | Negative | Non-PDF file type | Upload a 100 KB .jpg file | File is rejected and not stored |
| TC-06 | Negative | Empty PDF file | Upload a 0-byte file with .pdf extension | File is rejected and not stored |
| TC-07 | Negative | Empty non-PDF file | Upload a 0-byte file with .txt extension | File is rejected and not stored |
| TC-08 | Negative | Corrupted PDF | Upload a 100 KB file with .pdf extension but invalid PDF header | File is rejected and not stored (assuming content validation is part of "PDF files only") |

Questions, if needed
1. What specific error message or HTTP status code should be returned for each rejection type (wrong type, too large, empty)?
2. Does "PDF files only" imply content validation (checking magic bytes/header) or just file extension validation?

cases.review_notes: Adds PDF-header/content-validation rejection even though other validation rules are outside scope.

cases.requirement: In a project, an owner may invite members and remove other members. A member may view the member list but cannot invite or remove anyone. An unauthorised invite or removal must leave membership unchanged. The owner cannot remove their own membership.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover owner permissions, member viewing, blocked member invite/removal, unchanged membership after denial and blocked owner self-removal. Do not prescribe an HTTP status or interface unless supplied.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing core permission logic and state integrity. The main gap is the definition of "unauthorised" (e.g., does it include expired tokens or specific error codes?) and the expected system response (error message vs. silent failure) for denied actions.

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Owner invites a new member | Owner sends invite request for User B | User B is added to the member list with "Member" role |
| TC-02 | Normal | Owner removes an existing member | Owner sends remove request for User C | User C is removed from the member list |
| TC-03 | Normal | Member views member list | Member sends view list request | Member list is returned successfully |
| TC-04 | Negative | Member attempts to invite | Member sends invite request for User D | Invite is rejected; membership list remains unchanged |
| TC-05 | Negative | Member attempts to remove | Member sends remove request for User E | Removal is rejected; membership list remains unchanged |
| TC-06 | Boundary | Owner attempts to remove self | Owner sends remove request for their own ID | Removal is rejected; owner remains in the member list |
| TC-07 | Negative | Unauthorised user attempts invite | User with no role sends invite request | Invite is rejected; membership list remains unchanged |
| TC-08 | Negative | Unauthorised user attempts remove | User with no role sends remove request | Removal is rejected; membership list remains unchanged |

Questions, if needed
1. What is the specific expected system response (e.g., HTTP status code, error message) when an unauthorised action is attempted?
2. Does "unauthorised" include scenarios where a valid member's session has expired, or only users without the required role?

cases.review_notes: Assumes an invitation immediately adds the invitee as a Member; invitation completion behavior was not supplied.

cases.requirement: A booking starts as Pending. Only Pending bookings may be confirmed or cancelled. Confirming changes the state to Confirmed; cancelling changes it to Cancelled. Confirmed and Cancelled bookings reject further confirmation or cancellation requests and retain their state.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover both allowed transitions and both actions from each terminal state. Check that rejected actions leave the state unchanged. Do not add refund or notification behaviour.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement clearly defines the state machine transitions and rejection rules for Pending, Confirmed, and Cancelled states. No significant gaps affect the core logic testing.

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Confirm a pending booking | Booking state: Pending; Action: Confirm | State changes to Confirmed |
| TC-02 | Normal | Cancel a pending booking | Booking state: Pending; Action: Cancel | State changes to Cancelled |
| TC-03 | Negative | Confirm a confirmed booking | Booking state: Confirmed; Action: Confirm | Request rejected; State remains Confirmed |
| TC-04 | Negative | Cancel a confirmed booking | Booking state: Confirmed; Action: Cancel | Request rejected; State remains Confirmed |
| TC-05 | Negative | Confirm a cancelled booking | Booking state: Cancelled; Action: Confirm | Request rejected; State remains Cancelled |
| TC-06 | Negative | Cancel a cancelled booking | Booking state: Cancelled; Action: Cancel | Request rejected; State remains Cancelled |

cases.review_notes: Covers both allowed transitions and both actions from each terminal state while preserving state after rejection.

cases.requirement: A staff member can download an existing invoice as a PDF. The PDF must show the same invoice number and total as the stored invoice. The interface, download procedure and storage location will be supplied later.
cases.expected_behavior: Propose high-level download and content checks with a staff member and existing invoice as preconditions. Retain the known PDF and matching-value outcomes; ask for execution details without inventing buttons, URLs or paths.

result.text:
Requirement note
The core functional requirement is clear, but the specific UI interaction, file format details, and storage mechanism are missing, which limits the scope of interface-specific tests.

Candidate tests

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Download valid invoice | Select an existing invoice with a known number and total; trigger download. | A PDF file is generated and downloaded successfully. |
| TC-02 | Normal | Verify PDF content accuracy | Open the downloaded PDF from TC-01. | The PDF displays the exact same invoice number and total amount as the stored invoice record. |
| TC-03 | Negative | Attempt to download non-existent invoice | Trigger download for an invoice ID that does not exist in the system. | The system returns an appropriate error message; no PDF is generated. |
| TC-04 | Boundary | Invoice with maximum length fields | Download an invoice with the longest allowed invoice number and highest possible total value. | The PDF renders correctly without truncating the invoice number or total. |
| TC-05 | Negative | Download invoice with null/missing total | Attempt to download an invoice record where the total field is null or undefined. | The system handles the missing data gracefully (e.g., shows "N/A" or errors out) without crashing; PDF content reflects the stored state. |

Questions, if needed
1. What is the expected behavior if the invoice total is negative (e.g., credit notes)?
2. Are there specific font or layout requirements for the PDF that need to be verified?

cases.review_notes: Adds unsupported missing-invoice, maximum-field and null-total behavior beyond the supported download/content outcomes.

cases.requirement: A user can submit an expense claim with an amount and receipt. A positive amount and attached receipt are required; otherwise reject the claim without storing it. Valid claims are stored as Pending. Treatment of a second submission with the same receipt has not been decided.
cases.expected_behavior: Cover valid Pending storage, non-positive amounts and missing receipts with no storage. Ask what should happen to duplicate receipts; do not prescribe rejection or acceptance for duplicates.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing validation logic and state transitions, but the handling of duplicate receipts is undefined, preventing tests for that specific scenario.

Candidate tests
| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Normal | Valid claim submission | Submit claim with amount > 0 and valid receipt attached | Claim is stored with status "Pending" |
| TC-02 | Negative | Zero amount | Submit claim with amount = 0 and valid receipt attached | Claim is rejected and not stored |
| TC-03 | Negative | Negative amount | Submit claim with amount < 0 and valid receipt attached | Claim is rejected and not stored |
| TC-04 | Negative | Missing receipt | Submit claim with amount > 0 and no receipt attached | Claim is rejected and not stored |
| TC-05 | Boundary | Minimum positive amount | Submit claim with smallest valid positive amount (e.g., 0.01) and valid receipt | Claim is stored with status "Pending" |

Questions, if needed
What is the expected behavior when a user submits a second claim using the same receipt ID? Should it be rejected, allowed, or flagged for review?

cases.review_notes: Covers valid/invalid claims and asks about duplicates, but describes 0.01 as an example of the smallest valid positive amount without a supplied granularity rule.

cases.requirement: Two current documents describe report access. Requirement A says only managers may download monthly reports. Requirement B says all signed-in users may download them. No precedence is specified. Both documents agree that signed-out users must be denied access.
cases.expected_behavior: Test manager access and signed-out denial where the sources agree. Identify the conflict for signed-in non-managers and ask which rule applies. Leave that outcome unresolved rather than choosing a document.

result.text:
**Requirement note**
The requirement is insufficiently clear for testing because there is a direct conflict between Requirement A and Requirement B regarding who can download reports, with no specified precedence. The only unambiguous behavior is that signed-out users must be denied access.

**Candidate tests**

| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-001 | Negative | Signed-out user attempts download | User is not authenticated; clicks "Download Monthly Report" | Access is denied; user is prompted to sign in or receives an error message. |
| TC-002 | Normal | Manager attempts download (per Req A) | User is authenticated as a Manager; clicks "Download Monthly Report" | Report downloads successfully. |
| TC-003 | Normal | Non-manager signed-in user attempts download (per Req B) | User is authenticated as a standard user (non-manager); clicks "Download Monthly Report" | Report downloads successfully. |
| TC-004 | Boundary | User with no role attempts download | User is authenticated but has no specific role assigned; clicks "Download Monthly Report" | Access is denied (assuming "signed-in" implies valid role, or clarify if role-less users are allowed). |

**Questions, if needed**
1. Which requirement takes precedence: Requirement A (Managers only) or Requirement B (All signed-in users)?
2. Are there any specific roles other than "Manager" that should be explicitly allowed or denied?

cases.review_notes: Provides a definite signed-in non-manager download outcome despite the unresolved access-rule conflict.

cases.requirement: In staging with 10,000 seeded products, run 100 concurrent virtual users for 10 minutes after a 2-minute warm-up. Each user sends one catalogue-search request every 5 seconds. During the measured 10 minutes, the 95th-percentile response time must be at most 800 ms and fewer than 1% of requests may fail.
cases.expected_behavior: Preserve the dataset, concurrency, request interval, warm-up and measured duration. Use p95 <= 800 ms and failure rate < 1%, not averages or altered boundaries. Ask for endpoint and failure definition if absent. Do not claim measured results.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is sufficiently clear for testing performance metrics and load parameters. The main gap is the definition of "failure" (e.g., HTTP 5xx, timeout, or specific error codes) and the exact search query parameters used by the virtual users.

Candidate tests
| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | Performance | 95th-percentile response time compliance | Run 100 concurrent users for 10 minutes (after 2-min warm-up) with 1 request per user every 5 seconds against 10,000 seeded products. | The 95th-percentile response time is â‰¤ 800 ms. |
| TC-02 | Reliability | Request failure rate compliance | Execute the same load profile as TC-01. | Fewer than 1% of total requests result in a failure (e.g., HTTP 5xx or timeout). |
| TC-03 | Boundary | Warm-up exclusion verification | Monitor system metrics during the first 2 minutes and the subsequent 10 minutes. | The 2-minute warm-up period is excluded from the calculation of the 95th-percentile response time and failure rate. |
| TC-04 | Negative | System stability under sustained load | Observe system resource usage (CPU, memory, DB connections) during the 10-minute measured period. | No resource exhaustion, crashes, or service interruptions occur; the system remains stable throughout the test. |

Questions, if needed
1. What specific HTTP status codes or error conditions are defined as a "failure" for the <1% threshold?
2. What specific search query parameters (e.g., keyword, category, pagination) should the virtual users use to ensure consistent load?

cases.review_notes: Preserves the stated load profile and thresholds but adds an unsupported absolute no-crashes/no-resource-exhaustion expectation.

cases.requirement: The checkout service should be reliable and easy to use. No workflows, measurable targets, implementation or execution evidence are supplied. Suggest what is needed to test it and say whether its quality can currently be confirmed.
cases.expected_behavior: Ask for checkout workflows, operating conditions, reliability targets and usability criteria. State that quality cannot yet be confirmed. Do not invent thresholds, payment methods, test results or an executable test table.

result.text:
Requirement note
The requirement is too vague to define specific test cases because it lacks measurable targets, functional specifications, and defined workflows. Quality cannot currently be confirmed as "reliable" and "easy to use" are subjective without objective criteria.

Candidate tests
| Test ID | Test type | Scenario | Input or action | Expected result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| N/A | N/A | Insufficient information | N/A | N/A |

Questions, if needed
1. What are the specific functional steps of the checkout workflow (e.g., cart review, payment method selection, confirmation)?
2. What are the measurable targets for "reliability" (e.g., 99.9% uptime, <2s response time, 0% transaction failure rate)?
3. What are the criteria for "easy to use" (e.g., maximum number of clicks, specific UI/UX guidelines, accessibility standards)?
4. What are the supported payment methods and error handling requirements (e.g., card declined, network timeout)?

cases.review_notes: States that quality cannot be confirmed and asks for workflows, conditions, reliability and usability criteria; example thresholds are posed as questions, not asserted requirements.

cases.requirement: In staging with 10,000 seeded products, run 100 concurrent virtual users for 10 minutes after a 2-minute warm-up. Each user sends one catalogue-search request every 5 seconds. During the measured 10 minutes, the 95th-percentile response time must be at most 800 ms and fewer than 1% of requests may fail.

result.text:
Requirement note

Execution detail needed: Specific load testing tool, script configuration, and how to extract the 95th-percentile metric from the results. |
